chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Abi Baseer, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who performs Tamattu', but cannot find a sacrificial animal, so he fasts the three days. So when he fulfills his ritual, it becomes evident to him that he should stay in Mecca. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should wait for the arrival of the people of his land. So when he thinks that they have entered, let him fast the seven days.'

key_terms.الثَّلَاثَةَ الْأَيَّامِ: The three days (of fasting in Mecca)
key_terms.السَّبْعَةَ الْأَيَّامِ: The seven days (of fasting in the hometown)
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: Performs Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are combined with a break in between)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim performing Tamattu' who cannot afford the sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural timing for the expiation (kaffarah) of Tamattu' Hajj, distinguishing between the three days fasted in Mecca and the seven days fasted upon return to one's hometown. Scholars emphasize the condition that the pilgrim must wait until the people of his city have arrived to ensure the fasts are completed in the proper location, reflecting the juristic precision of the Imami school. This ruling underscores the flexibility in fulfilling the ten-day fast when the sacrificial animal is unaffordable, prioritizing the completion of the ritual obligations.
